metadata.title: The Squire's Recipes: Being a Reprint of an Odd Little Volume As Done by Kendall Banning
metadata.author: Kendall Banning
metadata.notes: Libro publicado en 1912 por los Brothers of the Book en Chicago. Fue presentado como reimpresión de un volumen original de 1784 (un engaño literario admitido por Kendall Banning), conteniendo doce recetas con prosa de estilo colonial revolucionario americano, atribuidas al ficticio Squire Calvin Banning de Fairfield Manor.

sections.title: Explanation
sections.content_original: During a recent Christmas season, the friends of Kendall Banning received an odd little volume dated 1784, apparently worn with age, and entitled 'The Squire's Recipes.' In this musty book were printed, in quaint type, and in the picturesque language of the Revolutionary period, a dozen recipes for drinks, ranging from the old-fashioned cherry bounce to alluring wassails, swizzles, and the wicked 'pirate tipple.' Each recipe was preceded by a little story of how the doughty old New England squire, Calvin Banning, had originated the concoction. Tucked away in the fly leaves was a little note from Kendall Banning, great-grandson of the old Squire Calvin, to the effect that these books had been discovered in a moth-eaten hair-trunk in grandmother's attic in Connecticut, and had been bound and distributed to a few discerning comrades. The book attracted attention at once. Libraries sent in requests for it. Newspapers printed articles about the 'find'; one staid sheet published extracts from it that flooded the office with protests from prohibitionists from all over New England. An elderly relative wrote confidentially to Mr Banning that she had to confess to a sneaking regard for spirituous liquors, adding guilelessly, 'You doubtless know that grandfather was excommunicated from the church because of his fondness for them.' No; Mr Banning did not know. So, to save grandfather's reputation, Mr Banning had to admit that the book was a hoax. He had written it himself, printed it from old, battered type on paper that he had stained with coffee, and trampled upon to give semblance of age. With such minute attention to detail had the task been done that the book was taken at its face value by everyone but the expert. Only one hundred and fifty copies were printed, and the situation was further complicated because half of the edition bore the name of Squire Hoggson, great-grandfather of Noble Foster Hoggson, who supplied half of the recipes in the book, and who shared equally in the hoax. Except for the binding, which was designed for this edition by the writer of these lines, this book presents a faithful reproduction of the original, even to the carefully planned crudities resulting from the use of much worn type. — Laurence C. Woodworth, December, 1912.
sections.content_es: Durante una reciente temporada navideña, los amigos de Kendall Banning recibieron un curioso pequeño volumen fechado en 1784, aparentemente desgastado por el tiempo, titulado 'The Squire's Recipes'. En este mohoso libro se imprimieron, en una tipografía pintoresca y en el lenguaje pintoresco del período revolucionario, una docena de recetas de bebidas, desde el clásico cherry bounce hasta atractivos wassails, swizzles y el malvado 'pirate tipple'. Cada receta iba precedida por una pequeña historia sobre cómo el valiente y anciano squire de Nueva Inglaterra, Calvin Banning, había originado la mezcla. Escondida en las guardas había una pequeña nota de Kendall Banning, bisnieto del viejo Squire Calvin, indicando que estos libros habían sido descubiertos en un baúl de pelo apolillado en el desván de la abuela en Connecticut, y habían sido encuadernados y distribuidos a unos pocos camaradas perspicaces. El libro llamó la atención de inmediato. Las bibliotecas pidieron ejemplares. Los periódicos publicaron artículos sobre el 'hallazgo'; una hoja seria publicó extractos que inundaron la oficina con protestas de prohibicionistas de toda Nueva Inglaterra. Una pariente anciana le escribió confidencialmente al señor Banning confesando una furtiva afición por los licores espirituosos, añadiendo ingenuamente: 'Sin duda sabes que el abuelo fue excomulgado de la iglesia por su afición a ellos'. No; el señor Banning no lo sabía. Así pues, para salvar la reputación del abuelo, el señor Banning tuvo que admitir que el libro era una farsa. Lo había escrito él mismo, lo había impreso con tipos viejos y maltratados sobre papel que había manchado con café y pisoteado para darle apariencia de antigüedad. Con tan minuciosa atención al detalle se había realizado la tarea que el libro fue tomado al pie de la letra por todos excepto por el experto. Solo se imprimieron ciento cincuenta copias, y la situación se complicó aún más porque la mitad de la edición llevaba el nombre del Squire Hoggson, bisabuelo de Noble Foster Hoggson, quien suministró la mitad de las recetas del libro y compartió equitativamente la farsa. Salvo por la encuadernación, diseñada para esta edición por el autor de estas líneas, este libro presenta una reproducción fiel del original, incluso en las cuidadosamente planeadas imperfecciones resultantes del uso de tipos muy desgastados. — Laurence C. Woodworth, diciembre de 1912.

sections.title: Addenda
sections.content_original: The writer of the 'explanation' accepted Mr Banning's statement that the original of this reprint was a hoax. Since the book went to press, however, several of Mr Banning's friends have written in vigorous protest, maintaining that the hoax rests in Mr Banning's contention, and not in the book itself, which they assert was a genuine product of the year 1784. One friend insists that he was with Mr Banning when the original 'find' was made in the Connecticut attic. This writer is not concerned in this good-natured controversy, holding that the book is equally interesting whether viewed as a production of 1784 or 1911. The reader may take his choice! — L. C. W. Chicago, December 16, 1912.
sections.content_es: El autor de la 'explicación' aceptó la afirmación del señor Banning de que el original de esta reimpresión era una farsa. Sin embargo, desde que el libro fue a imprenta, varios amigos del señor Banning han escrito en vigorosa protesta, sosteniendo que la farsa está en la afirmación del señor Banning, y no en el libro mismo, el cual aseguran que fue un producto genuino del año 1784. Un amigo insiste en que estaba con el señor Banning cuando se hizo el 'hallazgo' original en el desván de Connecticut. Este escritor no se preocupa por esta controversia amistosa, sosteniendo que el libro es igualmente interesante ya sea visto como una producción de 1784 o de 1911. ¡El lector puede elegir! — L. C. W. Chicago, 16 de diciembre de 1912.

sections.title: Title Page (1784)
sections.content_original: THE SQUIRE'S RECIPES. In Which are Described the Methods by Which CALVIN BANNING, Esquire, Compounded the Twelve most Famous Toddies that Distinguished his Hospitality. HORACE: Spes donare novas largus amaraque, Curarum dulce efficax. SUDBURY. Printed by ROGER BUCK and sold at his shop in Cornhill, 1784.
sections.content_es: LAS RECETAS DEL SQUIRE. En las que se describen los métodos por los cuales CALVIN BANNING, Esquire, compuso los doce ponches más famosos que distinguieron su hospitalidad. HORACIO: 'Generoso al dar nuevas esperanzas y dulce remedio para las preocupaciones'. SUDBURY. Impreso por ROGER BUCK y vendido en su tienda en Cornhill, 1784.

sections.title: Preface
sections.content_original: These recipes are collected at the instance of the numerous friends of Calvin Banning, Esquire, sometimes known as Old Squire Banning, of whose hospitality they have partaken at his homestead, Fairfield Manor, situate at the crossroads of Pleasant Valley. For many years the Squire has devised both indoor and outdoor games and recreation for his friends and neighbours, and he has, in consequence, acted as host on numerous occasions where his toddies and other liquid refreshments have been potent factors in the course of entertainment. To those who have participated in the sports on his estate in summer, or who have gathered about his hearth during the winter evenings, these recipes of his most famous beverages will be welcomed reminders of passed delights; to those who have yet to taste the pleasures of his hospitality, promises of delights yet to come.
sections.content_es: Estas recetas se recopilan a instancias de los numerosos amigos de Calvin Banning, Esquire, a veces conocido como el Viejo Squire Banning, de cuya hospitalidad han disfrutado en su hogar, Fairfield Manor, situado en la encrucijada de Pleasant Valley. Durante muchos años, el Squire ha ideado juegos y recreaciones tanto de interior como de exterior para sus amigos y vecinos, y ha actuado en consecuencia como anfitrión en numerosas ocasiones en las que sus toddies y otras bebidas refrescantes han sido factores potentes en el desarrollo del entretenimiento. Para aquellos que han participado en los deportes de su finca en verano, o que se han reunido junto a su chimenea durante las veladas de invierno, estas recetas de sus bebidas más famosas serán bienvenidos recordatorios de delicias pasadas; para aquellos que aún tienen que probar los placeres de su hospitalidad, promesas de delicias por venir.

sections.title: Colophon (The End)
sections.content_original: Here ends this book, THE SQUIRE'S RECIPES, being a reprint of a certain hoax perpetrated on a time by one Kendall Banning, now produced in this form at the Lakeside Press in Chicago, and issued by the BROTHERS OF THE BOOK during December, Nineteen hundred and twelve.
sections.content_es: Aquí termina este libro, LAS RECETAS DEL SQUIRE, siendo una reimpresión de cierta farsa perpetrada en su tiempo por un tal Kendall Banning, ahora producido en esta forma en la Lakeside Press en Chicago, y publicado por los BROTHERS OF THE BOOK durante diciembre de mil novecientos doce.

ingredients.notes: para llenar el vaso hasta el borde

recipes.method_original: This beverage should be served in large, thin beakers, which should first be filled to the top with chipped ice. On top of the ice in each beaker, pour two ponies (one jigger) of old-fashioned apple jack, the juice of one lime and a spoonful of white sugar. Mix the ingredients well, fill the beaker with water and serve with straws, through which the potion should be sipped slowly.
recipes.method_es: Esta bebida debe servirse en vasos altos y delgados (beakers), que primero se llenan hasta el borde con hielo picado. Sobre el hielo de cada vaso, vierta dos ponies (un jigger) de apple jack a la antigua, el zumo de una lima y una cucharada de azúcar blanco. Mezcle bien los ingredientes, rellene el vaso con agua y sirva con pajitas, a través de las cuales la poción debe sorberse lentamente.
recipes.raw_text:
THE LIME JACK

This beverage should be served in large, thin beakers, which should first be filled to the top with chipped ice. On top of the ice in each beaker, pour two ponies (one jigger) of old-fashioned apple jack, the juice of one lime and a spoonful of white sugar. Mix the ingredients well, fill the beaker with water and serve with straws, through which the potion should be sipped slowly.

ingredients.notes: una pequeña cantidad esparcida sobre una rebanada de pan tostado

recipes.method_original: First, pour a gallon of boiling water over four pounds of honey. Set it to boil and skim it thoroughly. Add a quarter of a pound of best hops and again boil for ten minutes. Then allow it to cool in a clean wooden tub. When the concoction is nearly cool, add a small quantity of yeast, which should be spread on a slice of toasted bread. Allow this to stand in a warm room until the fermentation is finished. Then place it in a small cask and bung it tight, leaving a peg hole open for a few days. After pegging, allow the mead to stand for nine months. Then bottle it and store it safely within easy access, ready for use.
recipes.method_es: Primero, vierta un galón de agua hirviendo sobre cuatro libras de miel. Póngalo a hervir y espúmelo a fondo. Añada un cuarto de libra de los mejores lúpulos y vuelva a hervir durante diez minutos. Después, deje enfriar en una cuba de madera limpia. Cuando la mezcla esté casi fría, añada una pequeña cantidad de levadura esparcida sobre una rebanada de pan tostado. Deje reposar en una habitación cálida hasta que termine la fermentación. Después, póngalo en un barril pequeño y tape bien, dejando un agujero abierto unos días. Tras taponar, deje el hidromiel reposar durante nueve meses. Después, embotelle y guarde a salvo y al alcance, listo para usar.
recipes.glassware: barril pequeño para fermentar; embotellar al final
recipes.raw_text:
THE SCOTTISH MEAD

First, pour a gallon of boiling water over four pounds of honey. Set it to boil and skim it thoroughly. Add a quarter of a pound of best hops and again boil for ten minutes. Then allow it to cool in a clean wooden tub.

When the concoction is nearly cool, add a small quantity of yeast, which should be spread on a slice of toasted bread. Allow this to stand in a warm room until the fermentation is finished. Then place it in a small cask and bung it tight, leaving a peg hole open for a few days. After pegging, allow the mead to stand for nine months. Then bottle it and store it safely within easy access, ready for use.

recipes.name_es: El Cherry Bounce (Salud de la tarde)

ingredients.notes: primero hervidas para romper los huesos

recipes.method_original: To one quart of wild black cherries, add one gallon of good whiskey, first broiling the cherries, so as to break the stones. Then shell a handful of almonds and add to them a half tumbler of white sugar, a quarter of a spoonful of nutmeg, a quarter of a spoonful of cloves and a half spoonful of cinnamon, all of which should be bruised together in an earthen or metal pot. Let the compound stand a fortnight, and then draw off the liquid. Finally, add a half gallon of best brandy to it and preserve it in air-tight bottles, from which it should be served in nip glasses.
recipes.method_es: A un cuarto de galón de cerezas negras silvestres, añada un galón de buen whisky, hirviendo primero las cerezas para romper los huesos. Después pele un puñado de almendras y agregue medio vaso de azúcar blanco, un cuarto de cucharadita de nuez moscada, un cuarto de cucharadita de clavos y media cucharadita de canela; todo ello debe machacarse junto en una olla de barro o metal. Deje reposar la mezcla quince días, y después extraiga el líquido. Finalmente, añada medio galón del mejor brandy y consérvelo en botellas herméticas, desde las cuales debe servirse en copitas (nip glasses).
recipes.raw_text:
THE CHERRY BOUNCE

To one quart of wild black cherries, add one gallon of good whiskey, first broiling the cherries, so as to break the stones. Then shell a handful of almonds and add to them a half tumbler of white sugar, a quarter of a spoonful of nutmeg, a quarter of a spoonful of cloves and a half spoonful of cinnamon, all of which should be bruised together in an earthen or metal pot. Let the compound stand a fortnight, and then draw off the liquid. Finally, add a half gallon of best brandy to it and preserve it in air-tight bottles, from which it should be served in nip glasses.

recipes.name_original: The Tom and Jerry (A Fireside Nuggin)

ingredients.notes: cantidad igual a la del ron (cuatro jiggers)
rallada por encima antes de servir

recipes.method_original: This luscious potion requires six eggs, which should be duly mixed with eight spoonfuls of white sugar and well beaten. Next, add thereto four jiggers of Jamaica rum, an equal quantity of the best brandy and one and one-half pints of boiling water. Then serve it while still hot in earthenware mugs. On the top, before serving, should be distributed the gratings of a nutmeg. This quantity should be sufficient for the ordinary needs of six people.
recipes.method_es: Esta deliciosa poción requiere seis huevos, que deben mezclarse debidamente con ocho cucharadas de azúcar blanco y batirse bien. A continuación, añada cuatro jiggers de ron de Jamaica, una cantidad igual del mejor brandy y una pinta y media de agua hirviendo. Después, sírvalo aún caliente en jarras de barro. Por encima, antes de servir, debe distribuirse nuez moscada rallada. Esta cantidad debería ser suficiente para las necesidades ordinarias de seis personas.
recipes.raw_text:
THE TOM AND JERRY

This luscious potion requires six eggs, which should be duly mixed with eight spoonfuls of white sugar and well beaten. Next, add thereto four jiggers of Jamaica rum, an equal quantity of the best brandy and one and one-half pints of boiling water. Then serve it while still hot in earthenware mugs. On the top, before serving, should be distributed the gratings of a nutmeg. This quantity should be sufficient for the ordinary needs of six people.

ingredients.notes: machacadas en el vaso con una cuchara
preparado según la receta del propio libro
exprimir un pedazo sobre cada porción

recipes.method_original: Take a tall beaker and with a spoon, crush therein some fresh mint leaves. Then fill the beaker with cracked ice, and for each portion, add two ponies (one jigger) of dry gin, and one pony of lime syrup, which should be made after the manner hereinafter described. Stir these ingredients well, and through a strainer, pour the mixture into thin glass tumblers. Squeeze over each portion, a bit of orange peel and add a sprig of mint. LIME SYRUP: Mix the rind and juice of eighteen limes with one ounce of tartaric acid and three pounds of white sugar. Dissolve all in a pan over the fire (first adding a quart of water) and heat till it near boils. Then strain, cool and bottle the resultant syrup.
recipes.method_es: Tome un vaso alto (beaker) y con una cuchara, machaque en él unas hojas de menta fresca. Después llene el vaso con hielo picado y, por cada porción, añada dos ponies (un jigger) de ginebra seca y un pony de jarabe de lima, preparado según se describe a continuación. Remueva bien estos ingredientes y, a través de un colador, vierta la mezcla en vasos finos. Exprima sobre cada porción un trozo de cáscara de naranja y añada una ramita de menta. JARABE DE LIMA: Mezcle la cáscara y el zumo de dieciocho limas con una onza de ácido tartárico y tres libras de azúcar blanco. Disuelva todo en una sartén al fuego (añadiendo primero un cuarto de galón de agua) y caliente hasta que casi hierva. Después cuele, enfríe y embotelle el jarabe resultante.
recipes.glassware: vaso fino (thin glass tumbler), preparado en un beaker alto
recipes.garnish: cáscara de naranja exprimida y ramita de menta
recipes.raw_text:
THE PRIMROSE

Take a tall beaker and with a spoon, crush therein some fresh mint leaves. Then fill the beaker with cracked ice, and for each portion, add two ponies (one jigger) of dry gin, and one pony of lime syrup, which should be made after the manner hereinafter described. Stir these ingredients well, and through a strainer, pour the mixture into thin glass tumblers. Squeeze over each portion, a bit of orange peel and add a sprig of mint.

LIME SYRUP: Mix the rind and juice of eighteen limes with one ounce of tartaric acid and three pounds of white sugar. Dissolve all in a pan over the fire (first adding a quart of water) and heat till it near boils. Then strain, cool and bottle the resultant syrup.

recipes.method_original: To one jigger of a sweet Italian vermouth, add an equal quantity of sweet gin, preferably the Old Tom gin. Next, flavour with a slight portion of a sweet liqueur which the monks call Benedictine, to the amount of a mere dash. Shake these ingredients well together with cracked ice, and pour into a small glass, into which should be first placed a Maraschino cherry. This drink is sufficient for one person, and should be served only before eating. Because of its potency, it should be repeated cautiously.
recipes.method_es: A un jigger de vermut italiano dulce, añada una cantidad igual de ginebra dulce, preferiblemente Old Tom gin. A continuación, aromatice con una pequeña porción de un licor dulce que los monjes llaman Benedictine, en cantidad de una mera pizca. Agite bien estos ingredientes con hielo picado y vierta en un vaso pequeño, en el que previamente se habrá colocado una cereza al marrasquino. Esta bebida es suficiente para una persona y debe servirse sólo antes de comer. Por su potencia, debe repetirse con precaución.
recipes.raw_text:
THE DARTMOUTH DRACHM

To one jigger of a sweet Italian vermouth, add an equal quantity of sweet gin, preferably the Old Tom gin. Next, flavour with a slight portion of a sweet liqueur which the monks call Benedictine, to the amount of a mere dash. Shake these ingredients well together with cracked ice, and pour into a small glass, into which should be first placed a Maraschino cherry. This drink is sufficient for one person, and should be served only before eating. Because of its potency, it should be repeated cautiously.

recipes.method_original: For each person, use a large beaker and fill it with cracked ice. Squeeze into it the juice of one lime and add a sweet, golden-brown syrup known as Grenadine in quantities to suit the taste of the guest, usually about one pony. Then add one jigger of Irish whiskey, shake the concoction well together till it be thoroughly chilled, serve with straws and sip it slowly.
recipes.method_es: Por cada persona, use un vaso grande (beaker) y llénelo con hielo picado. Exprima dentro el zumo de una lima y añada un jarabe dulce y dorado conocido como granadina en cantidades al gusto del huésped, generalmente alrededor de un pony. Después añada un jigger de whisky irlandés, agite bien la mezcla hasta que esté completamente fría, sirva con pajitas y sorba lentamente.
recipes.raw_text:
THE IRISH ROSE

For each person, use a large beaker and fill it with cracked ice. Squeeze into it the juice of one lime and add a sweet, golden-brown syrup known as Grenadine in quantities to suit the taste of the guest, usually about one pony. Then add one jigger of Irish whiskey, shake the concoction well together till it be thoroughly chilled, serve with straws and sip it slowly.

ingredients.notes: una pieza grande en la ponchera

recipes.method_original: Brew a pint of strong lemonade. Add thereto one-half pint of apricot brandy and one pint of cognac. Stir these ingredients together and pour the concoction over a piece of ice that has just been placed in the punch bowl. Just before serving, add two quarts of chilled champagne and dress the bowl with fresh mint leaves, sliced oranges and seasonable fruits.
recipes.method_es: Prepare una pinta de limonada fuerte. Añada media pinta de brandy de albaricoque y una pinta de coñac. Remueva estos ingredientes juntos y vierta la mezcla sobre un trozo de hielo que se acaba de colocar en la ponchera. Justo antes de servir, añada dos cuartos de galón de champán frío y adorne el bol con hojas de menta fresca, rodajas de naranja y frutas de temporada.
recipes.garnish: hojas de menta fresca, rodajas de naranja y frutas de temporada
recipes.raw_text:
THE TAVERN TODDY

Brew a pint of strong lemonade. Add thereto one-half pint of apricot brandy and one pint of cognac. Stir these ingredients together and pour the concoction over a piece of ice that has just been placed in the punch bowl. Just before serving, add two quarts of chilled champagne and dress the bowl with fresh mint leaves, sliced oranges and seasonable fruits.

ingredients.notes: preparado a partir de una onza de té Oolong

ingredients.item_original: strawberries, pineapples, cherries or seasonable fruits
ingredients.item_es: fresas, piñas, cerezas u otras frutas de temporada

recipes.method_original: Take an earthen vessel and put into it the thin peel of twelve lemons and six oranges. Pour a pint of boiling water over them and let the mixture stand one hour. Then strain it into a punch bowl and add thereto some light-brown sugar to the taste. Add to this the juice of twenty-four lemons and six oranges, two quarts of Jamaica rum, two quarts of brandy, two quarts of Sauterne wine and one quart of tea, made from one ounce of Oolong. Place into this concoction strawberries, pineapples, cherries or other seasonable fruits, and a large piece of ice, and if desired, from two to three quarts of water. And remember that the punch weakens proportionate to the melting of the ice.
recipes.method_es: Tome una vasija de barro y ponga en ella la cáscara fina de doce limones y seis naranjas. Vierta una pinta de agua hirviendo sobre ellas y deje reposar la mezcla durante una hora. Después cuele en una ponchera y añada azúcar moreno claro al gusto. Agregue el zumo de veinticuatro limones y seis naranjas, dos cuartos de galón de ron de Jamaica, dos cuartos de galón de brandy, dos cuartos de galón de vino Sauternes y un cuarto de galón de té preparado con una onza de Oolong. Coloque en esta mezcla fresas, piñas, cerezas u otras frutas de temporada, y un trozo grande de hielo, y si se desea, de dos a tres cuartos de galón de agua. Y recuerde que el ponche se debilita en proporción al derretimiento del hielo.
recipes.garnish: fresas, piñas, cerezas u otras frutas de temporada y un trozo grande de hielo
recipes.raw_text:
THE SQUIRE'S PUNCH

Take an earthen vessel and put into it the thin peel of twelve lemons and six oranges. Pour a pint of boiling water over them and let the mixture stand one hour. Then strain it into a punch bowl and add thereto some light-brown sugar to the taste. Add to this the juice of twenty-four lemons and six oranges, two quarts of Jamaica rum, two quarts of brandy, two quarts of Sauterne wine and one quart of tea, made from one ounce of Oolong. Place into this concoction strawberries, pineapples, cherries or other seasonable fruits, and a large piece of ice, and if desired, from two to three quarts of water. And remember that the punch weakens proportionate to the melting of the ice.

ingredients.notes: dos pintas más, añadir cuando esté caliente

recipes.method_original: Core and roast six large apples, and keep them near at hand while compounding the following: a pint of ale, to which should be added a half pound of brown sugar, and a half ounce each of ginger, nutmeg and cinnamon. Heat this mixture slowly, stirring continuously, but be careful not to let it boil. When hot, add two more pints of ale, one half-pint of malaga and a little lemon peel. Then pour the compound into mugs, in each of which should be placed, at the last moment before serving, an apple, roasted just to the point whereat it bursts white and fleecy.
recipes.method_es: Descorazone y ase seis manzanas grandes, manteniéndolas cerca mientras prepara lo siguiente: una pinta de cerveza ale, a la que debe añadir media libra de azúcar moreno, y media onza de jengibre, nuez moscada y canela. Caliente esta mezcla lentamente, removiendo continuamente, pero teniendo cuidado de que no hierva. Cuando esté caliente, añada dos pintas más de cerveza ale, media pinta de vino de Málaga y un poco de cáscara de limón. Después vierta el compuesto en jarras, en cada una de las cuales debe colocar, en el último momento antes de servir, una manzana asada justo hasta el punto en que estalla blanca y esponjosa.
recipes.garnish: una manzana asada en cada jarra
recipes.raw_text:
THE FAIRFIELD WASSAIL

Core and roast six large apples, and keep them near at hand while compounding the following: a pint of ale, to which should be added a half pound of brown sugar, and a half ounce each of ginger, nutmeg and cinnamon. Heat this mixture slowly, stirring continuously, but be careful not to let it boil. When hot, add two more pints of ale, one half-pint of malaga and a little lemon peel. Then pour the compound into mugs, in each of which should be placed, at the last moment before serving, an apple, roasted just to the point whereat it bursts white and fleecy.

recipes.method_original: To eight bottles of a light Rhenish wine, add two bottles of Arrack and enough white sugar to suit the taste. Add a few sticks of cinnamon, a few whole cloves, and mix the concoction well in a metal vessel. Then heat a mulling stick (preferably one made with canister shot fastened to the end of a bent iron rod) until it be red hot, and plunge it into the mixture. This will burn off some of the alcohol and at the same time heat the punch. Care must be taken to place the metal vessel where the flames will not set fire to anything. This swizzle should be served in goblets while it is still hot.
recipes.method_es: A ocho botellas de un vino blanco del Rin ligero, añada dos botellas de arak y suficiente azúcar blanco al gusto. Añada unas cuantas ramas de canela, unos cuantos clavos enteros y mezcle bien en una vasija de metal. Después caliente una varilla de calentar (preferiblemente una hecha con perdigones de metralla sujetos al extremo de una varilla de hierro curvada) hasta que esté al rojo vivo, y sumérjala en la mezcla. Esto quemará parte del alcohol y al mismo tiempo calentará el ponche. Hay que tener cuidado de colocar la vasija metálica donde las llamas no incendien nada. Este swizzle debe servirse en copas mientras aún esté caliente.
recipes.raw_text:
THE MANOR SWIZZLE

To eight bottles of a light Rhenish wine, add two bottles of Arrack and enough white sugar to suit the taste. Add a few sticks of cinnamon, a few whole cloves, and mix the concoction well in a metal vessel.

Then heat a mulling stick (preferably one made with canister shot fastened to the end of a bent iron rod) until it be red hot, and plunge it into the mixture. This will burn off some of the alcohol and at the same time heat the punch. Care must be taken to place the metal vessel where the flames will not set fire to anything. This swizzle should be served in goblets while it is still hot.

recipes.method_original: Take seven ponies of Jamaica rum and add thereto four spoonfuls of sugar, one handful of browned coffee, three sticks of cinnamon, a half dozen of cloves and six pimento berries. Also, there might be added a few pieces of fresh orange peel. Place all of these ingredients together in a bowl and mix them well. Then set fire to the concoction and let it burn till it becomes hot, after which it should be served in rummers just before retiring for the night.
recipes.method_es: Tome siete ponies de ron de Jamaica y añada cuatro cucharadas de azúcar, un puñado de café tostado, tres ramas de canela, media docena de clavos y seis bayas de pimienta de Jamaica. También se pueden añadir unos pedazos de cáscara fresca de naranja. Coloque todos estos ingredientes juntos en un bol y mézclelos bien. Después prenda fuego a la mezcla y deje arder hasta que esté caliente, tras lo cual debe servirse en copas grandes (rummers) justo antes de retirarse a dormir.
